storage: append-only JSONL day-files under <archive>/pipeline_health/, one line per recorded snapshot (no gzip — plain rows stay tiny, ~150 bytes each)
written_by: server/pipelineHealthHistory.ts recordHealthSnapshot(), called from inside the existing /api/health handler (server/bot.ts) on every hit, throttled in-memory to one write per DEFAULT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS (5 min) — no dedicated poller/timer
source: the same /api/health computation the endpoint already returns to callers (Railway platform health checks + any external monitor) — this stream is a flattened snapshot of that response, not a separate fetch from anywhere
license: internal operational telemetry, no third-party terms

field_map.status: 'ok' | 'degraded' — the /api/health top-level status at that instant
field_map.scanner_ok / scanner_consecutive_failure: Tier-2 scan backoff state at snapshot time
field_map.bot_status / bot_liveness_dark: trading-loop active/stopped/killed state and the LIVENESS ALARM flag
field_map.heap_used_mb / rss_mb: Node process memory at snapshot time

confidence_model: RAW operational telemetry, no predictive claim — this is the PIPELINE-HEALTH panel (MAP V2 ROADMAP R6(c)), not a trading or product signal. uptime_pct is reported null (never fabricated as 100%) whenever a window has zero recorded samples.
entity_key: t (one row per recorded instant; no other stream to join against)
cadence: throttled to at most one write per 5 minutes, driven by whatever cadence /api/health is actually polled at
_note: Closes the R6 dashboard trio (R6(a) signal-strength + R6(b) data-quality shipped 2026-07-30 were pure joins over already-computed state; this one needed an actual time-series capture, which research/open_questions.md's roadmap note flagged as the reason (c) stayed unbuilt). Served at /api/data/pipeline-health-dashboard, rendered at #/data/pipeline-health.
